title: Montana State hosts campus preview for over 250 Montana high school seniors
text:
Waded Cruzado President of Montana State University | Montana State University
Waded Cruzado President of Montana State University | Montana State University
About 257 high school seniors from 60 towns across Montana attended Montana State University’s STATE Days, a two-day campus preview event designed for in-state students. The event, which began on July 31, aimed to introduce prospective students and their families to the university through campus tours, overnight stays in Hyalite Hall, meals with faculty and staff, and information sessions tailored to student interests.
Shannon Bangen, associate director of new student programs at MSU, expressed her hopes for attendees: “I hope that after attending STATE Days, students leave not only excited about MSU but also confident that pursuing a college degree is within reach — and that they’ll be supported every step of the way.”
Participants toured key campus facilities such as Jabs Hall and the Student Wellness Center. Kayla Young, an MSU senior from Belgrade who guided groups during the event, shared insights about student traditions and available resources. She highlighted her own experience using state-based scholarships and pursuing multiple degrees at MSU. “We have programs to keep you afloat,” Young said. “MSU wants you here, and we’ll support you any way we can.”
Information sessions included details about scholarship opportunities like the Hilleman Scholarship for Montanans demonstrating leadership potential and the presidential scholarships for academic achievement and public service. Ronak Kommineni, a Bozeman high school senior interested in these scholarships, spoke about his research experiences at MSU: “[At MSU,] we extract cartilage from samples, and we use the DNA to see if there’s specific metabolite markers that can be seen in unhealthy versus healthy knees,” he said.
Bangen underscored MSU’s strong record in national scholarship competitions during her welcome speech: “We are among institutions such as Harvard, Princeton and — we're ahead of a school, let’s see if I can pronounce this correctly — Yale,” she told attendees.
While many families traveled less than half an hour to attend STATE Days due to their proximity to Bozeman, some drove over five hours from rural areas with small graduating classes. Logan Bloom traveled from Missoula to explore both aerospace engineering and medical fields at MSU. Makayla Oberly of Bozeman attended to learn more about pre-veterinary studies while appreciating the affordability of the free event.
Oberly commented on MSU’s focus on supporting local students: “It shows MSU cares for their Montana residents,” she said. “It makes us feel like a priority.”
